speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning. I see you have a complex history; could you describe exactly how your gait and limb coordination have changed over time? Did you experience any episodes of loss of consciousness or falls?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description. Has this clumsiness been constant, or do you notice it gets worse with movement or in specific situations? Also, do you experience any double vision, difficulty speaking, or numbness in your hands or feet?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. Given your history of Crohn's disease and the onset of ataxia while on this medication, this is a known but serious risk. I recommend immediate MRI of the brain and Oligoclonal Band testing.
